    1. API Reference
    2. Prompts & Runtime

    Runtime API Reference¶

    Agent process lifecycle, triggers, governance (budget, health, mission, secrets), journals, distributed coordination, and the orchestration API.

    Core¶

    AgentProcess¶

    promptise.runtime.process.AgentProcess ¶

    Lifecycle container for a long-running agent process.

    Lifecycle (see :mod:promptise.runtime.lifecycle): :meth:start, :meth:stop, :meth:suspend / :meth:resume, automatic restarts (restart_policy) and :meth:close. Every lifecycle change emits an event when an event_notifier is set: process.started, process.stopped, process.failed (with the error), process.restarted, process.restart_exhausted, process.suspended and process.resumed (both with a reason: "manual", "idle", "budget", "health", "rewind" or, for an automatic resume, "trigger").

    Trigger events are processed in arrival order. While the process is suspended they wait in the queue; at :meth:stop the events still queued (or held by a worker, or running) are moved to :attr:dead_letters with reason "process stopped", from where :meth:redeliver_dead_letters can queue them again after a restart.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    name str

    Unique process name.

    		 required
    config ProcessConfig

    Process configuration.

    		 required
    process_id str | None

    Unique ID (auto-generated if not provided).

    		 None
    event_bus Any | None

    Optional shared EventBus for inter-process events.

    		 None
    broker Any | None

    Optional shared MessageBroker for message triggers.

    		 None
    runtime Any | None

    Optional parent :class:AgentRuntime reference (enables the spawn_process meta-tool in open mode).

    		 None
    event_notifier Any | None

    Optional :class:~promptise.events.EventNotifier for the process's events (and its agent's).

    		 None
    hooks HookManager | None

    Optional shared :class:~promptise.runtime.hooks.HookManager (e.g. one :class:AgentRuntime passes to all its processes), dispatched after the process's own :attr:hooks (which holds config.hooks); ctx.process_id names the process.

    		 None
    deploy_policy DeployPolicy | None

    Where the config came from (:class:~promptise.runtime._deploy_policy.DeployPolicy). The default is an operator config without limits; the control API passes source="api", which limits ${VAR} references in secrets to the variables the operator allowed and makes an empty open_mode.allowed_mcp_urls mean no MCP server. Processes this one spawns get the same policy.

    		 None
    extra_tools Sequence[Any] | None

    Local tools for the agent, added after config.extra_tools (same kinds as :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent's extra_tools: :func:promptise.tool functions, plain functions and LangChain tools). They go through the same budget, approval, health and journal checks as MCP tools and are kept on every rebuild of the agent. Anything that is not a tool raises TypeError here.

    		 None
    model Any | None

    The agent's model, used instead of config.model: a model id, or a model object as :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent takes it (a LangChain chat model such as promptise.testing.ScriptedModel, a :class:promptise.Model, a :class:~promptise.FallbackChain). Every agent the process builds uses it, and so does the mission evaluator. Anything else raises ValueError here.

    		 None

    Lifecycle hooks: the process dispatches every :class:~promptise.runtime.hooks.HookEvent to :attr:hooks (see the event's docstring for when, with which data, and what blocking it does). Hook data has secret values redacted.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    An entry of config.servers is not a server spec (see :func:_resolve_server_specs), or model is not a model.
    TypeError

    An entry of extra_tools is not a tool or function.
    context property ¶

    The unified agent context.

    dead_letters property ¶

    Trigger events that could not be processed, oldest first.

    Each entry has event (the :class:TriggerEvent), reason ("retries exhausted", "process failed", "process stopped", "process restarting", "trigger removed", "queue full", "flagged by payload scan", "blocked by guardrails" or "blocked by hook"), error, attempts and dead_lettered_at. A stop dead-letters every event not run yet: queued, held by a worker or a trigger listener, or still inside a trigger (a file watch's backlog, a webhook's accepted requests). The list keeps the most recent trigger_delivery.dead_letter_size entries.

    hooks property ¶

    This process's :class:~promptise.runtime.hooks.HookManager.

    Holds the hooks of config.hooks; register more in code::

    @process.hooks.on(HookEvent.USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT)
async def audit(ctx):
    ...

    Its default hook timeout is 30 seconds. A hook must not await a lifecycle method of this process (stop(), start(), rewind()); schedule it with asyncio.create_task.

    lifecycle property ¶

    The lifecycle state machine (for inspection).

    model property ¶

    The model the process's agent runs on: the model given to the constructor, else config.model (an id or a model object).

    recovered property ¶

    What the first :meth:start restored from the journal, or None.

    Keys: lifecycle_state (the state the journal last recorded: "stopped" after a clean stop, "running" after a crash), entries_replayed, context_keys, mission_restored, budget_restored, conversation_messages, invocation_count and interrupted_runs (runs a stop cancelled, back in :attr:dead_letters).

    spawned_processes property ¶

    Names of the processes this one spawned (open mode).

    state property ¶

    Current process state.

    suspend_reason property ¶

    Why the process is suspended ("manual", "idle", "budget", "health", "rewind"), or None when it isn't.

    abort_drain() ¶

    End a graceful stop's wait now: the runs in flight are cancelled.

    For a second SIGTERM / Ctrl+C during stop(drain_timeout=...). Does nothing when no stop is waiting.

    add_dynamic_trigger(config) async ¶

    Add a trigger on the agent's behalf (open mode's add_trigger).

    Unlike :meth:add_trigger the trigger is not added to config.triggers: it lives until :meth:stop, :meth:rollback or :meth:remove_trigger, and counts towards open_mode.max_dynamic_triggers. It starts at once with its listener (and filter). A CONFIG_CHANGE hook (source="agent", change="trigger_added") can refuse it.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    str

    The trigger's ID.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    RuntimeError

    Not in open mode, or the process is stopping, stopped or failed.
    PermissionError

    open_mode.allow_trigger_management is off, a hook refused it, or it is a webhook on a non-loopback host (see :meth:_agent_trigger_problem).
    ValueError

    The limit is reached, or the config is invalid or can't start.
    add_trigger(config) async ¶

    Add a config trigger; it starts at once if the process is active.

    The trigger is appended to config.triggers. A RUNNING or SUSPENDED process creates and starts it immediately (its events queue while suspended); otherwise it starts with the next :meth:start.

    Name Type Description Default

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    str

    The trigger's stable ID (see :func:config_trigger_ids).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    The config is invalid or the trigger can't be created or started. Nothing is added.
    apply_governance_config(section) ¶

    Apply config.<section> to the running process now.

    Call it after changing config.budget, config.health or config.mission (the orchestration API's PATCH routes do). Enabling a subsystem builds it, disabling it drops it, and new values of an enabled one apply from its next check: the budget keeps its counters, the health monitor its history (:meth:HealthMonitor.apply_config) and the mission its progress. The next invocation uses the updated callbacks; one already running finishes with the old ones.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    section str

    "budget", "health" or "mission".

    		 required

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    section is not one of those.

    clear_dead_letters() ¶

    Drop all dead letters. Returns how many were removed.

    close() async ¶

    Stop the process and release what lives as long as the object.

    Calls :meth:stop, then closes the long-term memory provider, revokes secrets (whatever revoke_on_stop says) and clears the conversation history. async with process: and :meth:AgentRuntime.remove_process call it. A closed process can be started again: :meth:start opens a new memory provider (an in_memory one starts empty).

    remove_trigger(trigger_id, *, source='operator') async ¶

    Stop and remove a trigger: a config trigger or an agent-added one.

    A config trigger (ID from :func:config_trigger_ids) is removed from config.triggers and, when it runs, stopped with its listener at once. An agent-added (open mode) trigger is stopped, its listener cancelled, and dropped. The other triggers keep their IDs. Dispatches CONFIG_CHANGE (change="trigger_removed").

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    trigger_id str

    The trigger's ID.

    		 required
    source str

    "operator" (default) or "agent" (the open-mode remove_trigger meta-tool): an agent can only remove triggers it added, and a CONFIG_CHANGE hook can refuse it.

    		 'operator'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    KeyError

    No trigger has trigger_id (for source="agent": no agent-added one).
    PermissionError

    A hook refused the agent's change.
    resume(*, reason='manual') async ¶

    Resume a SUSPENDED process (or one in the reserved AWAITING).

    Queued events run in arrival order, and the idle clock restarts, so idle_timeout counts from the resume. Emits process.resumed with the reason and suspended_for (the reason of the suspension).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    reason str

    event woke a process suspended for idle_timeout) or "rewind" (the end of a :meth:rewind).

    		 'manual'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    StateError

    The process is not suspended.
    rewind(target_entry_id, mode='both', *, actor='operator', wait_timeout=60.0) async ¶

    Roll the process back to just before a journal entry.

    Modes (:class:~promptise.runtime.journal.RewindMode): "both" (context state and conversation history), "conversation_only", "code_only" (the context state only), "summarize" (nothing is rolled back; a system note about the interval is added to the conversation) and "cancel" (a dry run, like :meth:rewind_plan).

    Non-destructive: the journal is only appended to — a rewind entry (with actor) and a checkpoint of the rewound state, so a later recovery starts from it. Never rolled back: long-term memory, the budget counters (a rewind doesn't refund budget), the mission, secrets, and the effects tool calls had outside the process.

    A RUNNING process is suspended for the rewind (reason "rewind"), waits for a run in flight to finish, and is resumed afterwards; events that arrive meanwhile wait in the queue. A suspended or stopped process stays as it is. Emits process.rewound and the CONFIG_CHANGE hook (change="rewind").

    Different from :meth:rollback (open mode), which discards the agent's self-modifications (instructions, tools, servers, triggers) and keeps the state and history.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    target_entry_id str

    The journal entry to go back to (from GET /processes/{name}/journal or :meth:JournalProvider.read); the state is rebuilt as it was just before it.

    		 required
    mode Any

    The rewind mode.

    		 'both'
    actor str

    Who asked (recorded in the journal).

    		 'operator'
    wait_timeout float

    Seconds to wait for a run in flight.

    		 60.0

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    The Any

    Raises:

    Type Description
    RuntimeError

    The process has no journal.
    ValueError

    Unknown entry or mode.
    TimeoutError

    A run was still in flight after wait_timeout (nothing was changed; the process is resumed).
    rewind_plan(target_entry_id, mode='both') async ¶

    Preview :meth:rewind without changing anything.

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    A Any
    Any

    journal entries after the target the rewind would undo).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    RuntimeError

    The process has no journal.
    ValueError

    target_entry_id is not in the journal, or mode is not a :class:~promptise.runtime.journal.RewindMode.
    rollback() async ¶

    Revert to the original configuration (open mode).

    Clears all dynamic state (instructions, tools, servers, triggers) and rebuilds the agent from the original config. It undoes the agent's self-modifications; it doesn't touch the context state or the conversation history. To roll those back to an earlier point, use :meth:rewind (any mode). A rollback is not refused by OpenModeConfig.max_rebuilds (it is how an operator undoes the agent's changes), but it counts as a rebuild. If the rebuild fails, the instructions, tools and servers are restored and the previous agent is kept.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    str

    Status message.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    RuntimeError

    If called in strict mode.

    set_dynamic_instructions(instructions) async ¶

    Replace the instructions on the agent's behalf (open mode).

    What the modify_instructions meta-tool calls: the agent is rebuilt with instructions (hot reload), :meth:rollback restores the configured ones, and open_mode.max_instruction_length / max_rebuilds apply. A CONFIG_CHANGE hook (source="agent") can refuse it. Operators use :meth:update_instructions instead.

    Returns:

    "Rebuild successful" or an "Error: ..." message.

    Raises:

    spawn_process(name, *, instructions, model=None, triggers=None, execution_mode=ExecutionMode.STRICT, runtime=None) async ¶

    Spawn a process in the runtime on the agent's behalf (open mode).

    What the spawn_process meta-tool calls. The new process is registered in the parent :class:AgentRuntime and started; it inherits this process's guardrails (see :meth:_child_config), its hooks (the parent's :attr:hooks, and what the parent itself inherited, are dispatched for the child after its own, so permission_request and user_prompt_submit hooks govern the child too) and its deploy policy (a child of an API-deployed process is limited like its parent). Webhook triggers for the child must listen on loopback unless open_mode.allow_public_webhooks is on (then with an hmac_secret). Dispatches SUBAGENT_START first (a hook can refuse the spawn) and SUBAGENT_STOP when the child stops or fails. runtime overrides the process's own runtime reference.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    RuntimeError

    Not in open mode, or no runtime.
    PermissionError

    open_mode.allow_process_spawn is off, a hook refused the spawn, or a trigger is a webhook on a non-loopback host.
    ValueError

    max_spawned_processes reached, the name is taken, or the config is invalid.
    Exception

    The child failed to start (it is removed again).
    start() async ¶

    Build agent, start triggers, begin processing.

    Transitions: CREATED → STARTING → RUNNING (or STOPPED/FAILED → STARTING → RUNNING on restart).

    Starting a FAILED process first tears down what the failed run left (trigger listeners, triggers, heartbeat, agent), and cancels a pending automatic restart, so nothing runs twice.

    On the first start of the process object, when the journal holds a checkpoint for this process name and journal.recover_on_start is on (the default), the recorded context state, mission, conversation history and invocation count are restored first (see :attr:recovered).

    Raises:

    Type Description
    StateError

    If the transition is invalid (a :class:~promptise.runtime.exceptions.ProcessStateError and a :class:ValueError).

    Serializable status snapshot.

    last start; None while stopped or failed), triggers
    dict[str, Any]

    (id, type — the config type, e.g. "cron" —,
    dict[str, Any]

    source and, for a file watch, dropped_events
    dict[str, Any]

    and pending_events; for an event or message trigger,
    dict[str, Any]

    dropped_events), recovered (after a journal
    dict[str, Any]

    recovery) and, per enabled subsystem, budget,
    dict[str, Any]

    health_anomalies and health
    dict[str, Any]

    (:meth:HealthMonitor.health_status), mission_state and
    dict[str, Any]

    active_secrets; hook_count is the number of hooks on
    dict[str, Any]
    stop(*, drain_timeout=0.0) async ¶

    Transitions: RUNNING / SUSPENDED / STARTING / FAILED → STOPPING → STOPPED (emits process.stopped), or CREATED → STOPPED for a process that never started (no event). Stopping a stopped process does nothing.

    Trigger events still queued, held by a suspended worker or running are moved to :attr:dead_letters (reason "process stopped"). A run in flight is cancelled at once by default. With drain_timeout the stop is graceful: no new event starts (the triggers' events and :meth:inject go to the dead letters, a webhook answers 503), the runs in flight get up to that many seconds to finish, and only the ones still running then are cancelled.

    A cancelled run's event (error "run cancelled") may have had tool calls with effects already. It is journaled as a run_interrupted entry and kept in the journal checkpoint, so the next process object with the same name and journal lists it in :attr:dead_letters again after :meth:start.

    Secrets are revoked unless secrets.revoke_on_stop is False. Long-term memory, the context state and the conversation history are kept (unless context.conversation_clear_on_stop), so a later :meth:start continues where this one stopped; :meth:close releases them.

    An explicit stop also cancels any pending automatic restart.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    drain_timeout float | None

    Seconds to let runs in flight finish before cancelling them. 0 (default) cancels them at once; None uses config.drain_timeout (what :meth:AgentRuntime.run_forever does on SIGTERM).

    		 0.0
    suspend(*, reason='manual') async ¶

    Pause processing without tearing down the agent.

    Triggers continue to fire; their events wait in the queue, in order, and run after :meth:resume. A run in flight finishes. Emits process.suspended with the reason.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    reason str

    dashboard), "idle" (idle_timeout; the next trigger event resumes the process by itself), "budget", "health" or "rewind" (:meth:rewind suspends a running process while it rewinds, then resumes it).

    		 'manual'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    StateError

    The process is not RUNNING.
    update_instructions(instructions) ¶

    Replace the agent's instructions from the next invocation on.

    The next invocation rebuilds the agent with instructions before it runs (reusing the connected MCP tools); an invocation already running finishes with the old instructions. A process that is not running uses them when it starts. They replace any instructions an open-mode agent set for itself, and :meth:rollback keeps them.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    instructions str

    The new system prompt.

    		 required

    AgentRuntime¶

    promptise.runtime.runtime.AgentRuntime ¶

    Multi-process agent runtime manager.

    Manages a dictionary of :class:AgentProcess instances with shared resources and coordinated lifecycle.

    The processes declared in config.processes are registered at construction (not started): AgentRuntime(config) and :meth:from_config are equivalent.

    async with AgentRuntime(...) stops and closes every process on exit. Signals are not handled there: use :meth:run_forever (or call :meth:request_shutdown from your own handler) so SIGTERM shuts the runtime down cleanly instead of killing it mid-run.

    Distributed mode: with config.distributed.enabled, :meth:start_all (and :meth:run_forever) first start this node's management transport and, per the config, the cluster coordinator or the registration with one (see :class:~promptise.runtime.config.DistributedConfig; :attr:cluster). :meth:shutdown stops them.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    config RuntimeConfig | None

    Optional :class:RuntimeConfig for global settings and the processes to register.

    		 None
    event_bus Any | None

    Optional shared EventBus for inter-process events.

    		 None
    broker Any | None

    Optional shared MessageBroker for message triggers.

    		 None
    event_notifier Any | None

    Optional :class:~promptise.events.EventNotifier shared by all processes (drained by :meth:stop_all).

    		 None
    hooks Any | None

    Optional :class:~promptise.runtime.hooks.HookManager shared by all processes: its hooks fire for every process's lifecycle events (after each process's own hooks; ctx.process_id names the process).

    		 None
    cluster property ¶

    The running :class:~promptise.runtime.distributed.node.ClusterNode (its transport, coordinator, node_id, url), or None when distributed mode is off or not started.

    restart_process(name, *, stop_timeout=30.0) async ¶

    Restart a single process (stop then start).

    A running or suspended process is stopped first; a FAILED one is torn down by :meth:AgentProcess.start itself (its old triggers, listeners and heartbeat end before new ones start), so nothing fires twice. Context state, long-term memory and the conversation history carry over.

    A process that is already stopping (another stop or restart in progress) is waited for, up to stop_timeout seconds.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    name str

    Process name.

    		 required
    stop_timeout float

    Seconds to wait for a stop in progress.

    		 30.0

    Raises:

    Type Description
    KeyError

    If the process does not exist.
    RuntimeError

    The process was still stopping after stop_timeout seconds (nothing was started).
    run_forever(*, install_signal_handlers=True, drain_timeout=None) async ¶

    Start all processes and run until shutdown is requested.

    Returns after :meth:request_shutdown, SIGTERM or SIGINT (with install_signal_handlers), or when the task running it is cancelled; every process is then stopped and closed (:meth:shutdown), so docker stop or Ctrl+C never cuts a process off without process.stopped, a final checkpoint and its dead letters.

    The stop is graceful: no new trigger event starts, and runs in flight get up to drain_timeout seconds to finish before they are cancelled (a cancelled run is journaled, see :meth:AgentProcess.stop). A second signal during that wait cancels them at once.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    install_signal_handlers bool

    Install SIGTERM / SIGINT handlers on the running loop for the duration of the call (removed afterwards: SIGTERM goes back to the default, SIGINT to KeyboardInterrupt). Skipped where the loop doesn't support them (Windows, or a thread other than the main one).

    		 True
    drain_timeout float | None

    Seconds runs in flight may take to finish at shutdown. None (default) uses each process's config.drain_timeout (5 seconds unless set); 0 cancels them at once. request_shutdown(drain_timeout=...) replaces it for that shutdown.

    		 None
    shutdown(*, drain_timeout=0.0) async ¶

    Stop every process (:meth:stop_all), then close them all.

    Closing releases what a process keeps across restarts (long-term memory, secrets, conversation history). The processes stay registered. The cluster node (distributed mode) stops last.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    drain_timeout float | None

    How long runs in flight may finish first (see :meth:stop_all; default 0: cancel them at once).

    		 0.0
    start_all() async ¶

    Start all registered processes that are not running.

    CREATED, STOPPED and FAILED processes are started (a failed one is torn down first, see :meth:AgentProcess.start). A process that fails to start is logged and skipped. With distributed.enabled the cluster node starts first (:meth:start_distributed); its failure raises.

    AgentContext¶

    promptise.runtime.context.AgentContext ¶

    Unified context layer for an agent process.

    Provides:

    • .get() / .put() — persistent key-value state with audit trail
    • .memory — optional :class:~promptise.memory.MemoryProvider
    • .env — filtered environment variables
    • .files — mounted file paths

    Every successful write (:meth:put, :meth:update) is recorded in the key's audit history and handed to the hooks registered with :meth:add_update_hook. :meth:restore_state loads recovered state without firing them.

    Configuration¶

    ProcessConfig¶

    promptise.runtime.config.ProcessConfig ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Configuration for a single agent process.

    Composes all atomic configs and adds process-level settings.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    model Any

    The agent's model: a model id (e.g. openai:gpt-5-mini), or in code a model object as :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent takes it (a LangChain chat model such as promptise.testing.ScriptedModel, a :class:promptise.Model, a :class:~promptise.FallbackChain). A model object is code only, like extra_tools: model_dump() and to_dict() leave model out, so a config read back from them has the default model id. Anything else raises a ValidationError.
    instructions str | None

    System prompt for the agent.
    agent_pattern Any | None

    The reasoning pattern the agent runs, as in :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent: a pattern name from promptise.agent.AGENT_PATTERNS ("react", "managed", "code-action", "verify", "peoatr", "research", "autonomous", "deliberate", "debate") or, in code, a :class:~promptise.engine.PromptGraph. None (default) runs ReAct. An unknown name raises a ValidationError when the config is created. A graph object is code only, like a model object: model_dump() and to_dict() leave it out.
    servers dict[str, Any]

    MCP server specifications (same format as .superagent).
    triggers list[TriggerConfig]

    Trigger configurations.
    journal JournalConfig

    Journal configuration. Off by default (level="none"); pass a :class:JournalConfig to record transitions, invocations and checkpoints (JournalConfig() itself defaults to level="checkpoint").
    context ContextConfig

    AgentContext configuration.
    concurrency int

    Max concurrent trigger invocations.
    heartbeat_interval float

    Heartbeat period in seconds.
    idle_timeout float

    Seconds of inactivity before suspending (0 = never).
    max_lifetime float

    Max process lifetime in seconds (0 = unlimited).
    max_consecutive_failures int

    Consecutive failures before FAILED state.
    restart_policy Literal['always', 'on_failure', 'never']

    When to restart the process automatically. on_failure restarts it after it enters FAILED (e.g. max_consecutive_failures reached); always also restarts it when it stops itself at max_lifetime. An explicit :meth:~AgentProcess.stop never triggers a restart.
    drain_timeout float

    Seconds a graceful stop lets runs in flight finish before cancelling them (default 5). :meth:AgentRuntime.run_forever (SIGTERM, SIGINT) and stop(drain_timeout=None) use it; a plain :meth:~AgentProcess.stop cancels at once. Keep it below the platform's kill deadline (docker stop sends SIGKILL after 10 seconds by default).
    max_restarts int

    Max consecutive restart attempts after failures. The count resets after a successful invocation.
    restart_backoff float

    Delay in seconds before the first restart attempt; doubles on each consecutive attempt (capped at 60s).
    trigger_delivery TriggerDeliveryConfig

    Retries, dead-letter list and payload scanning for trigger events.
    guardrails Any | None

    Passed through to :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent when the agent is built, as are observe, cache, optimize_tools, adaptive and max_invocation_time.
    hooks list[HookConfig]

    Runtime lifecycle hooks (:class:HookConfig), registered on the process's :attr:~AgentProcess.hooks manager when the process is created.
    extra_tools list[Any]

    Local tools the agent can call next to the MCP servers' tools, as in :func:~promptise.agent.build_agent: functions made tools with :func:promptise.tool, plain functions (made tools as if decorated with @tool) and LangChain BaseTool instances. Budget, approval, health and journal apply to them as to MCP tools, and every rebuild of the agent (restart, hot reload, new instructions) keeps them. Code only, like :attr:HookConfig.callback: not serialised (to_dict() and model_dump() leave them out), and a manifest or YAML config can't set them. Anything that is not a tool raises TypeError when the config is created.

    Unknown keys are rejected, so a misspelt option fails loudly instead of being ignored.

    DistributedConfig¶

    promptise.runtime.config.DistributedConfig ¶

    Bases: _WarnOnUnknownKeys

    Distributed runtime coordination (RuntimeConfig.distributed).

    With enabled=True, :meth:AgentRuntime.start_all (and :meth:~AgentRuntime.run_forever) start this node's management transport (:class:~promptise.runtime.distributed.RuntimeTransport) on transport_host:transport_port; :meth:AgentRuntime.shutdown stops it. Then, depending on the role:

    • coordinator=True: this runtime hosts the cluster coordinator (:class:~promptise.runtime.distributed.RuntimeCoordinator), which monitors the nodes' health. With discovery_method="registry" nodes register themselves at POST /cluster/nodes of its transport (and are dropped when they stop re-registering for node_timeout seconds); with "static" the nodes are listed in static_nodes. The coordinator also lists itself.
    • coordinator_url set: this node registers with the coordinator at that URL when it starts, re-registers every heartbeat_interval seconds (so a restarted coordinator finds it again) and unregisters at shutdown.
    • Neither: a stand-alone node, managed through its transport (a static coordinator elsewhere can list it).

    Security: one cluster token (auth_token) authenticates everything: requests to this node's transport (every route but GET /health), this node's registration with the coordinator, and the coordinator's requests to the nodes. A non-loopback transport_host or a coordinator on another host needs it, unless allow_unauthenticated=True says a proxy or a private network authenticates callers.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    enabled bool

    Start the transport (and coordination) with the runtime.
    coordinator bool

    This runtime hosts the coordinator.
    coordinator_url str | None

    Base URL of the coordinator's transport, for discovery_method="registry" nodes.
    node_id str | None

    This node's ID (default: <hostname>-<port>).
    transport_host str

    Interface the transport binds (default loopback).
    transport_port int

    Port of the transport (0: a free port).
    advertise_url str | None

    URL other nodes reach this one at (default http://<transport_host>:<port>; required when binding a wildcard address and registering with a coordinator).
    auth_token SecretStr | None

    The cluster bearer token, or an ${ENV_VAR} reference resolved when the transport starts.
    allow_unauthenticated bool

    Allow a non-loopback transport or coordinator without auth_token.
    discovery_method Literal['registry', 'static', 'multicast']

    "registry" (nodes register with the coordinator) or "static" (static_nodes). "multicast" is not implemented and is rejected.
    static_nodes dict[str, str]

    node_id -> URL of the nodes, for a static coordinator.
    allowed_node_hosts list[str]

    For a registry coordinator: the host names or IP addresses a registering node's URL may name (*. + a domain matches its subdomains). Empty: any host. The coordinator sends the cluster token to every registered URL (health checks, management calls), so a token holder could point it anywhere; list your nodes' hosts to stop that.
    heartbeat_interval float

    Seconds between the coordinator's health checks and between a node's re-registrations.
    node_timeout float | None

    Seconds without a successful health check (or a re-registration) before a node counts as unhealthy (or is dropped from the registry). Default 3 * heartbeat_interval.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    An inconsistent combination (each message says what to change). In 1.4.3 and earlier these fields were read by nothing.

    Unknown keys are ignored with a FutureWarning.

    effective_node_timeout() ¶

    node_timeout, or three heartbeat intervals.

    Give the agent an update_state(key, value) tool that writes to its context state (limited to writable_keys when set). Off by default: without writable_keys the agent can write any key.
    file_mounts dict[str, str]

    Mapping of logical name → filesystem path.
    env_prefix str

    Only expose environment variables with this prefix (:meth:AgentContext.get_env). Must not be empty: an empty prefix would expose the whole environment.
    initial_state dict[str, Any]

    Pre-populated key-value state.

    Unknown keys are ignored with a FutureWarning.

    ExecutionMode¶

    promptise.runtime.config.ExecutionMode ¶

    Bases: str, Enum

    Agent execution mode.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    STRICT

    Agent cannot modify itself. Current behavior, default.
    OPEN

    Agent can adapt identity, memory, tools, and triggers at runtime — a self-evolving, autonomous agent.

    OpenModeConfig¶

    promptise.runtime.config.OpenModeConfig ¶

    Bases: _WarnOnUnknownKeys

    Guardrails for open execution mode.

    Controls what the agent is allowed to self-modify and how far. Only takes effect when ProcessConfig.execution_mode is :attr:ExecutionMode.OPEN.

    Security: open mode gives the model control over its own setup, so treat every allow_* capability as something the model (and whoever can put text in front of it: trigger payloads, inbox messages, tool results) can use. allow_tool_creation runs model-written Python inside the runtime's process; the restricted builtins are not a sandbox and can be escaped, so it amounts to running arbitrary code as the runtime's user. The control API refuses such deploys unless allow_command_deploys is on.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    allow_identity_change bool

    Agent can modify its own instructions.
    allow_tool_creation bool

    Agent can define new Python tools, executed in the runtime's process (not isolated; see above).
    allow_mcp_connect bool

    Agent can connect to new MCP servers.
    allow_trigger_management bool

    Agent can add/remove triggers.
    allow_memory_management bool

    Agent can explicitly store/search/forget.
    max_custom_tools int

    Max number of agent-created tools.
    max_dynamic_triggers int

    Max number of dynamically added triggers.
    max_instruction_length int

    Max character length for modified instructions.
    max_rebuilds int | None

    Max agent rebuilds (hot reloads) per lifetime of the process object; restarts do not reset it. A change the limit refuses is not applied, now or after a restart. rollback() is not refused. None = unlimited.
    allowed_mcp_urls list[str]

    The MCP server URLs the agent may connect to. Empty means any public URL for an operator-configured process (loopback, private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused; a warning is logged at start) and none for a process deployed through the control API. Listed URLs are trusted as written, private addresses included.
    identity_mcp_urls list[str]

    Agent-connected MCP servers that may receive the process identity's credential (identity) and a caller's token. Empty (the default): none do, so the agent can't send its credential to a server it picked.
    sandbox_custom_tools bool

    Run agent-written tools with restricted builtins and no imports (False: a fixed allowlist of standard-library imports). Either way the code runs in the runtime's process; this is not a security boundary.
    allow_process_spawn bool

    Agent can spawn new processes within the runtime. Defaults to False.
    max_spawned_processes int

    Max number of processes this agent can spawn.
    allow_public_webhooks bool

    Webhook triggers the agent adds, or gives a process it spawns, may bind a non-loopback webhook_host (they must then set hmac_secret). False (default): such triggers are refused.

    Unknown keys are ignored with a FutureWarning.

    Extra attempts for an event whose agent run raised. 0 (default) never retries. A retry re-runs the whole agent turn, so tools with side effects may run twice — only enable it when those tools are idempotent or gated by approval.
    retry_backoff float

    retry_backoff_max float

    scan_payloads bool

Uses ProcessConfig.guardrails when it is a scanner, otherwise an injection-only :class:~promptise.guardrails.PromptiseSecurityScanner (needs transformers; the model loads when the process starts).
    max_payload_chars int

    Longest payload rendering placed in the prompt; longer payloads are truncated with a marker.

See :mod:promptise.runtime.hooks for the events, what each one's data holds and which ones can be blocked.

    ProcessState¶

    promptise.runtime.lifecycle.ProcessState ¶

    AWAITING is reserved: :class:~promptise.runtime.process.AgentProcess never enters it (see the module docstring).

    ProcessLifecycle¶

    promptise.runtime.lifecycle.ProcessLifecycle ¶

    State machine for process lifecycle.

    Tracks the current state, validates transitions against :data:VALID_TRANSITIONS, and records an audit trail of all transitions. Transitions are serialised with an :class:asyncio.Lock, so concurrent tasks of one event loop can use it; it is not thread-safe.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    initial ProcessState

    Starting state (default :attr:ProcessState.CREATED).

    		 CREATED
    process_id str | None

    Owner name shown in :class:StateError messages.

    		 None 
    lc = ProcessLifecycle()
assert lc.state == ProcessState.CREATED

await lc.transition(ProcessState.STARTING, reason="user requested")
await lc.transition(ProcessState.RUNNING)

assert len(lc.history) == 2
    history property ¶

    Chronological list of all transitions.

    state property ¶

    Current process state.

    add_listener(listener) ¶

    Register a callback invoked after every successful transition.

    Listeners run in registration order, outside the state lock, so they may inspect :attr:state (and even trigger further transitions). A listener that raises is logged and skipped; it never undoes the transition.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    listener TransitionListener

    Sync or async callable receiving the :class:ProcessTransition.

    		 required
    can_transition(target) ¶

    Check whether transitioning to target is valid.

    Reconstruct a :class:ProcessLifecycle from a snapshot dict.

    Serializable snapshot of current state and full history.

    VALID_TRANSITIONS¶

    VALID_TRANSITIONS (promptise.runtime.lifecycle, also exported from promptise.runtime) maps each ProcessState to the frozenset of states it may move to. ProcessLifecycle.transition() checks it. The table is on Process Lifecycle.

    Triggers¶

    TriggerConfig¶

    promptise.runtime.config.TriggerConfig ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Configuration for a single trigger.

    Each trigger type requires a different subset of fields. The :meth:_validate_trigger_fields model validator enforces this for built-in types, and rejects bad cron expressions, time zones, filter expressions and source ranges when the config is created rather than when the process first runs. Custom trigger types use the custom_config dict. Unknown keys are rejected, so a misspelt option fails loudly instead of being ignored.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    type str

    Trigger type (built-in or custom-registered via :func:~promptise.runtime.triggers.register_trigger_type).
    cron_expression str | None

    Cron expression (cron type only). Five fields, or six with a trailing seconds field ("* * * * * */10" fires every 10 seconds).
    cron_timezone str | None

    IANA time zone the cron expression is read in (cron only). None means UTC.
    webhook_path str

    URL path for the webhook endpoint (webhook only).
    webhook_port int

    Listening port (webhook only).
    webhook_host str

    Interface to bind (webhook only). Defaults to 127.0.0.1 (loopback); use 0.0.0.0 to accept requests from other machines.
    hmac_secret SecretStr | None

    Shared secret for request signatures (webhook only). When set, unsigned or wrongly signed requests get 401. With signature_scheme="telegram" it is the secret_token given to Telegram's setWebhook (1-256 characters: letters, digits, _ and -).
    signature_scheme Literal['generic', 'github', 'stripe', 'telegram']

    How the signature is computed and sent: generic (X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hex>), github (X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>), stripe (Stripe-Signature: t=<ts>,v1=<hex> over "<ts>.<body>") or telegram (X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token: <secret>, the secret itself, compared in constant time).
    signature_header str | None

    Header carrying the signature. Defaults to the scheme's standard header.
    signature_tolerance int

    Max age in seconds of a timestamped (stripe) signature, to stop replays.
    allowed_sources list[str]

    Client IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to call the webhook (empty = any). Others get 403.
    webhook_max_body_bytes int

    Largest request body the webhook accepts, in bytes (webhook only, default 1 MiB). Larger bodies get 413.
    watch_path str | None

    Directory to watch (file_watch only).
    watch_patterns list[str]

    Glob patterns (file_watch only), matched against the file name.
    watch_events list[str]

    Filesystem events to react to (file_watch only): any of created, modified, deleted, moved.
    watch_debounce_seconds float

    Window in which events for the same file are merged into one (file_watch only).
    watch_recursive bool

    Also watch subdirectories (file_watch only, default True).
    watch_backend Literal['auto', 'watchdog', 'polling']

    How changes are detected (file_watch only): "auto" (native OS notifications through watchdog when it is installed, otherwise polling), "watchdog" (fail if it isn't installed) or "polling" (scan the directory every watch_poll_interval seconds; use it for network shares and bind mounts, where OS notifications are unreliable).
    watch_poll_interval float

    Seconds between scans with the polling backend (file_watch only).
    watch_max_pending_events int

    How many changed files the trigger holds while the process is busy (file_watch only). Events wait for the process instead of being dropped; changes to a file that is already waiting are merged into its event. Only when this many different files are waiting is a new one dropped, with an error log and a count in FileWatchTrigger.dropped_events.
    event_type str | None

    EventBus event type string (event only).
    event_source str | None

    Optional source filter (event only).
    topic str | None

    MessageBroker topic (message only).
    custom_config dict[str, Any]

    Additional key-value configuration for custom trigger types.
    filter_expression str | Callable[..., Any] | None

    Cheap pre-filter evaluated before the agent runs (all types, optional). Either a safe expression string such as "payload['action'] == 'opened'" (see :mod:promptise.runtime.triggers.filters) or a callable that takes the :class:~promptise.runtime.triggers.base.TriggerEvent and returns a bool. Events that don't match are skipped.
    trusted bool

    Deliver this trigger's payloads to the agent as the user's request instead of as untrusted data (all types, default False). By default a payload is wrapped in a block the agent is told not to take instructions from; with trusted=True it is not, so whoever can send this trigger an event directs the agent as its user does. Use it only for a trigger whose sender is authenticated, such as a chat webhook with hmac_secret: a webhook trigger without hmac_secret can't be trusted (ValueError), and the process logs a warning for a trusted file_watch, event, message or custom trigger, whose senders it can't verify. The payload scan (scan_payloads) and guardrails still apply.

    Setting an option that belongs to another built-in trigger type (for example watch_path on a cron trigger) is an error, since the trigger would ignore it.

    effective_signature_header property ¶

    The header the webhook reads the signature from.

    BaseTrigger¶

    promptise.runtime.triggers.base.BaseTrigger ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Protocol for all trigger implementations.

    Triggers produce :class:TriggerEvent objects that cause the agent process to invoke the agent. They run as background tasks and must be safely cancellable.

    A trigger that buffers events may also implement drain_pending() -> list[TriggerEvent]: after :meth:stop, the process takes those events and dead-letters them (on a restart: queues them for the restarted process) instead of losing them.

    start() async ¶

    Start listening for trigger conditions.

    stop() async ¶

    Stop the trigger and release resources.

    wait_for_next() async ¶

    Block until the next trigger event occurs.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    TriggerEvent

    The next :class:TriggerEvent.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    CancelledError

    If the trigger is stopped.
    TriggerError

    If the trigger encounters a fatal error.

    WebhookTrigger¶

    promptise.runtime.triggers.webhook.WebhookTrigger ¶

    HTTP webhook trigger.

    Starts an aiohttp server that listens for incoming POST requests and converts them to :class:TriggerEvent objects.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    path str

    URL path to listen on (e.g. "/webhook").

    		 '/webhook'
    port int

    TCP port to bind to.

    		 9090
    host str

    Host/IP to bind to. Defaults to "127.0.0.1" (loopback only). Set to "0.0.0.0" when external services or other nodes need to reach this webhook.

    		 '127.0.0.1'
    hmac_secret str | None

    Optional HMAC secret for signature verification. When set, requests without a valid signature get 401. Verification uses timing-safe comparison. Strongly recommended when host is not loopback. Without it, a loopback webhook refuses browser-style cross-site requests (421 for a non-loopback Host, 403 for a cross-site Origin).

    		 None
    signature_scheme Literal['generic', 'github', 'stripe', 'telegram']

    "generic", "github", "stripe" or "telegram" (see the module docs).

    signature_header str | None

    signature_tolerance int

    Max age in seconds of a stripe timestamp.

    allowed_sources list[str] | None

    InProcessEventBus¶

    promptise.runtime.triggers.event.InProcessEventBus ¶

    An event bus that delivers to subscribers in the same Python process.

    Implements what the runtime uses a bus for: subscribe / unsubscribe (event triggers) and emit (escalations with an event_type, :class:~promptise.events.EventBusSink). Nothing leaves the process: to reach other hosts, pass your own bus to :class:~promptise.runtime.AgentRuntime.

    Example::

    bus = InProcessEventBus()
runtime = AgentRuntime(event_bus=bus)
await bus.emit("pipeline.error", {"job": "nightly"}, source="etl")
    emit(event_type, data, source='') async ¶

    Deliver an event to every subscriber of event_type.

    A handler that raises is logged and does not stop the others.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    int

    How many subscribers it was delivered to.
    subscribe(event_type, handler) async ¶

    Call handler with every event of event_type.

    subscriber_count(event_type) ¶

    How many handlers are subscribed to event_type.

    unsubscribe(event_type, handler) async ¶

    Stop calling handler (no error if it was not subscribed).

    HealthConfig¶

    promptise.runtime.config.HealthConfig ¶

    Bases: _WarnOnUnknownKeys

    Behavioral health monitoring configuration.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    enabled bool

    Enable health monitoring for this process.
    stuck_threshold int

    Same tool+args N times in a row = stuck.
    loop_window int

    Tool calls to examine for loop detection.
    loop_min_repeats int

    Min pattern repeats to trigger.
    empty_threshold int

    N consecutive trivial final replies = anomaly.
    empty_max_chars int

    A final reply of at most this many characters (after stripping whitespace) is trivial. With the default 10, a 10-character reply counts as empty and an 11-character one doesn't; 0 counts only blank replies.
    error_window int

    Number of recent invocations the error rate is computed over. The rate is checked once the window is full.
    error_rate_threshold float

    An error rate at or above this (0–1) in a full window is an anomaly.
    on_anomaly Literal['log', 'pause', 'escalate', 'stop']

    What the process does when a run produced an anomaly (a health.anomaly event is emitted in every case): "log" logs it; "pause" suspends the process; "escalate" sends the escalation notification to escalation (when set) and suspends the process; "stop" stops the process.
    cooldown float

    Seconds before the same anomaly (same kind and same evidence: the same stuck call or loop) is reported again. Set 0 to report every repeat, e.g. for an in-run guard. :meth:HealthMonitor.clear_anomalies resets it.
    escalation EscalationTarget | None

    Escalation target for anomalies.

    Window sizes can be changed on a running monitor (for example with PATCH /api/v1/processes/{name}/health); the monitor resizes its windows and keeps the recorded data. Unknown keys are ignored with a FutureWarning.

    HealthMonitor¶

    promptise.runtime.health.HealthMonitor ¶

    Lightweight behavioral health analysis.

    All detection methods are pure logic — no I/O, no LLM calls. The same anomaly is reported at most once per cooldown seconds, to avoid spam. "The same" means the same kind and the same evidence: the same repeated call (stuck), the same repeating sequence (loop), or the same signal (empty responses, error rate). A different stuck call or loop is a new anomaly and is reported at once.

    To use the monitor as an in-run guard that acts on every repeat (a pre_tool hook that blocks the call while the agent is stuck), set cooldown=0: :meth:record_tool_call then returns the anomaly on each call that continues it.

    Window sizes follow the config: when error_window, loop_window, stuck_threshold or empty_threshold change on the config object the monitor reads (as PATCH /health does), the windows are resized on the next recorded call, keeping the most recent data. Call :meth:apply_config to switch to a different :class:HealthConfig object.

    The anomaly history keeps the latest :attr:MAX_ANOMALIES anomalies; the per-type counts in :meth:health_status count all of them.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    config HealthConfig

    Health monitoring configuration.

    		 required
    process_id str

    Owning process ID.

    		 required
    anomalies property ¶

    Detected anomalies, oldest first (the latest :attr:MAX_ANOMALIES).

    config property ¶

    The configuration the monitor reads.

    latest_anomaly property ¶

    Most recent anomaly, or None.

    tool_history property ¶

    Recent tool call history [(name, args_hash)].

    apply_config(config) ¶

    Switch to config, resizing the windows and keeping the data.

    The most recent tool calls, reply lengths and error flags are kept (as many as fit the new windows), as are the anomaly history and the cooldowns. The new thresholds apply from the next recorded call.

    begin_invocation() ¶

    Start a new invocation: forget the previous run's tool calls.

    Stuck and loop detection look for repetition within a run. A scheduled agent that calls the same tool once per run (e.g. a queue check every minute) is behaving normally, so tool history does not carry over between invocations. Response lengths and the error window do carry over: "three empty replies in a row" and "half the recent runs failed" are cross-run signals.

    clear_anomalies() ¶

    Forget detected anomalies and reset their cooldowns.

    After a clear, the next occurrence of any anomaly is reported at once (not only after cooldown), counts start from zero and the monitor reports healthy. The tool-call, reply-length and error windows are kept: they are evidence, not reports.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    int

    The number of anomalies that were in the history.
    from_dict(data, config, *, process_id='recovered') classmethod ¶

    Reconstruct from a journal checkpoint.

    health_status() ¶

    Health summary (public API; JSON-safe).

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict[str, Any]

    is_healthy (no anomaly reported within the last
    dict[str, Any]

    cooldown seconds), anomaly_count (total reported since
    dict[str, Any]

    the start or the last :meth:clear_anomalies),
    dict[str, Any]

    anomalies_by_type and latest_anomaly (type, description,
    dict[str, Any]

    ISO timestamp) or None.
    record_error() async ¶

    Record a failed invocation and check error rate.

    record_response(content) async ¶

    Record the agent's final reply and check for empty responses.

    Pass the reply the agent gave at the end of an invocation, not tool results: a tool returning [] is not an empty response. A reply of at most empty_max_chars characters (after stripping whitespace) counts as empty.

    record_success() async ¶

    Record a successful invocation.

    A run that itself produced an anomaly (a stuck or loop pattern during its tool calls) is not a recovery, even when it finished.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    bool

    True if this success clears a previous anomaly (recovery).
    record_tool_call(tool_name, args) async ¶

    Record a tool call and check for stuck/loop anomalies.

    take_new_anomalies() ¶

    Return the anomalies detected since the previous call.

    Each anomaly is returned once. AgentProcess calls this when a run ends (successfully or not) to apply on_anomaly to what the run produced, however long ago in the run it was detected.

    to_dict() ¶

    Serialise for journal checkpointing.

    Unknown keys are ignored with a FutureWarning.

    MissionTracker¶

    promptise.runtime.mission.MissionTracker ¶

    Tracks mission progress across invocations.

    Handles evaluation scheduling, LLM-as-judge calls, programmatic checks, timeout/limit checking, and context prompt generation.

    completed and failed are final: a judge verdict that arrives after the mission was failed (for example by POST /mission/fail while an evaluation was running) doesn't change it. Only an active mission can be paused; only a paused one resumed.

    The tracker keeps the latest :attr:MAX_EVALUATIONS evaluations. Its state round-trips through :meth:to_dict and :meth:restore (or :meth:from_dict), so a process can carry the mission across a restart: invocation count, elapsed time, state, failure reason and evaluation history.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    config MissionConfig

    Mission configuration.

    		 required
    process_id str

    Owning process ID.

    		 required
    journal JournalProvider | None

    Optional journal provider for logging evaluations.

    		 None
    success_check Callable[[MissionEvidence], bool | None] | None

    Optional callable (MissionEvidence) -> bool | None. Return True for achieved, False for not achieved, None for inconclusive (fall through to LLM evaluator).

    		 None
    evaluation_count property ¶

    Total evaluations performed (including ones no longer kept).

    evaluations property ¶

    Evaluations performed so far, oldest first (the latest :attr:MAX_EVALUATIONS).

    A failed mission stays failed.

    Run a mission evaluation.

    If a success_check callable is configured, it runs first. If it returns True → mission achieved. False → not achieved. None → fall through to LLM evaluator.

    If the LLM call fails, returns a safe default evaluation (achieved=False, confidence=0.5).

    Remove all secrets from the in-memory store.

    Called on process stop. Overwrites values with null bytes as a best-effort measure (Python's immutable strings mean the original value may persist in the interpreter's memory pool until garbage-collected). Retired values are discarded too, so :meth:sanitize_text no longer knows any value afterwards.

    rotate(name, new_value, *, ttl=None) async ¶

    :meth:sanitize_text applied to every string in a nested value.

    Dicts (keys and values), lists and tuples are walked; other values are returned unchanged. Returns a new object, the input is not modified.

    sanitize_text(text) ¶

    Replace secret values found in text with [REDACTED].

    Redacts current values and values that were replaced by :meth:rotate or expired (the last :data:MAX_RETIRED_VALUES per secret), longest first. The runtime uses it to keep secret values out of the journal; call it on any text you log or show.

    MessageInbox¶

    promptise.runtime.inbox.MessageInbox ¶

    Async-safe inbox for human-to-agent messages.

    Provides a bounded, priority-sorted queue with TTL-based expiry, per-sender rate limiting, and question/response tracking.

    When the inbox holds max_messages messages, adding one removes an answered question if there is one, otherwise evicts the oldest message of the lowest priority present. Critical messages are never evicted, and a message is never added in place of one with a higher priority: if every message in the inbox is critical, or the new message has a lower priority than every evictable one, the new message is refused with :class:InboxFullError. The inbox never holds more than max_messages messages.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    max_messages int

    Maximum messages in the inbox.

    		 50
    max_message_length int

    Maximum characters per message; longer content is truncated.

    		 2000
    default_ttl float

    Default time-to-live in seconds (0 = no expiry).

    		 3600
    max_ttl float

    Maximum allowed TTL in seconds (0 = no cap).

    		 86400
    rate_limit_per_sender int

    Maximum messages per sender per hour (messages without sender_id are not limited).

    		 20
    scanner Any | None

    Optional guardrail scanner (an object with scan_text(text, direction=...) such as :class:~promptise.guardrails.PromptiseSecurityScanner, or with check_input(text)). When set, :meth:add refuses content it flags with :class:InboxMessageRejected.

    		 None
    add(message) async ¶

    Add a message to the inbox.

    Content longer than max_message_length is truncated. The expiry is set from default_ttl when the message has none, and capped at max_ttl.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    message InboxMessage

    The message to add.

    Empty content, unknown priority or type.

    The scanner flagged the content.

    The inbox is full and nothing can be evicted.
    InboxRateLimitError

    The sender exceeded its hourly limit.
    All four subclass
    clear() async ¶

    Clear all messages.

    Whoever waits for the answer to a cleared question gets :class:InboxQuestionRemoved (in 1.4.3 and earlier the wait was cancelled, which dropped an /ask request's connection).

    get_pending() async ¶

    Get all non-expired pending messages, sorted by priority.

    Returns messages in order: critical → high → normal → low, then by timestamp (oldest first within same priority). Questions that were already answered are left out. Does NOT remove messages — call :meth:remove_consumed after the agent has seen them.

    get_questions() async ¶

    Get pending questions that haven't been answered yet.

    mark_processed(message_id) async ¶

    Mark a message as processed (remove from inbox).

    Questions are kept until their response is submitted.

    purge_expired() async ¶

    Remove all expired messages. Returns count removed.

    remove_consumed(delivered) async ¶

    Remove the messages a run consumed.

    Call after a run with the messages that were placed in its prompt (the list from :meth:get_pending). Directives, context and corrections are removed: the agent has seen them. Questions are removed once answered (see :meth:submit_response); unanswered questions stay until they are answered or expire.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    int

    How many messages were removed.
    rescan() async ¶

    Scan the messages already held with :attr:scanner; remove flagged ones.

    For a scanner attached after messages arrived (a process attaches its payload scanner when it starts, and a created process already takes messages). A removed question's waiter gets :class:InboxMessageRejected.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[tuple[str, str]]

    (message_id, reason) of every removed message (empty
    list[tuple[str, str]]

    without a scanner).

    Get inbox status summary (answered questions are not pending).

    Journal¶

    JournalConfig¶

    promptise.runtime.config.JournalConfig ¶

    Bases: _WarnOnUnknownKeys

    Journal (durable audit log) configuration.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    level Literal['none', 'checkpoint', 'full']

    Detail level — none (disabled), checkpoint (state snapshots per cycle), or full (every side effect).
    backend Literal['file', 'memory']

    Storage backend.
    path str

    Directory for the file backend.
    recover_on_start bool

    On a process object's first :meth:start, when the journal holds a checkpoint for the process name, restore what it recorded: the context state (with the context_update entries written after the checkpoint), the mission, the budget counters (so a restart can't reset the daily limits), the conversation history and the invocation count. Recovered keys replace the same keys of context.initial_state. A clean :meth:stop writes a checkpoint too, so the next run continues from it. True by default (a journal is opt-in, and recovery is what it is for); False always starts fresh.

    FileJournal¶

    promptise.runtime.journal.FileJournal ¶

    JSONL-based journal for durable process audit logging.

    One JSONL file per process, append-only writes. Checkpoints are stored separately in a JSON file.

    Parameters:

    journal = FileJournal("/tmp/journals")

    process_id="p-1",
    entry_type="trigger_event",
    data={"trigger_type": "cron"},
))
entries = await journal.read("p-1")
    append(entry) async ¶

entries = await journal.read("p-1")
assert len(entries) == 1

    Orchestration API¶

    Remote HTTP control of running processes.

    OrchestrationAPI¶

    promptise.runtime.api.OrchestrationAPI ¶

    REST API server for managing an AgentRuntime.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    runtime Any

    The :class:AgentRuntime to manage.

    		 required
    host str

    Bind address (default 127.0.0.1).

    		 '127.0.0.1'
    port int

    Port to listen on (default 9100).

    		 9100
    auth_token str | None

    Bearer token required on every route except GET /api/v1/health. Required when host is not a loopback address. "${VAR}" reads it from the environment.

    		 None
    on_shutdown Callable[[], Any] | None

    Enables POST /api/v1/runtime/shutdown (authenticated like every route): the request is answered 202 {"status": "shutting_down"} and on_shutdown (a sync or async callable) is called right after, e.g. runtime.request_shutdown. It is called without arguments, or with drain_timeout=<seconds> when the request body has one; a callable that takes no drain_timeout makes such a request 422 INVALID_FIELD. Without it the route doesn't exist (404). promptise runtime start uses it for promptise runtime stop.

    		 None
    allow_command_deploys bool

    Let POST /api/v1/processes deploy processes that run programs on this host: stdio MCP servers (command) and command hooks. Off by default, because anyone with the token could then run any command as the runtime's user; such a deploy answers 403 COMMANDS_NOT_ALLOWED. Turn it on only when every token holder may run commands here. Processes already in the runtime (loaded from manifests by the operator) are not checked. Open mode with open_mode.allow_tool_creation counts as running commands (the agent's create_tool is not sandboxed).

    		 False
    allow_env_references bool

    Let deployed configs use ${VAR} references to any environment variable of this host (in secrets, which the agent can read back). Off by default: such a config answers 403 ENV_REFERENCES_NOT_ALLOWED.

    		 False
    allowed_env_vars Iterable[str] | None

    The variables deployed configs may reference when allow_env_references is off, e.g. {"SEARCH_API_KEY"}.

    		 None
    data_dir str | Path | None

    The directory deployed configs' file system paths must lie in: journal.path (file journal), context.memory_persist_directory and file-watch watch_path (also those the deployed agent adds later). Relative paths are resolved against the working directory, as the process uses them. Default: ./.promptise (where the journal goes by default). Others answer 403 PATH_NOT_ALLOWED.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    auth_token is empty, names an unset environment variable, or host is not a loopback address and there is no auth_token.
    port property ¶

    The port the API listens on.

    With port=0 the OS picks a free port; after :meth:start this returns the port actually bound.

    start() async ¶

    Start the API server.

    stop() async ¶

    Stop the API server.

    OrchestrationClient¶

    promptise.runtime.api_client.OrchestrationClient ¶

    Async client for the Promptise Orchestration API.

    Provides typed methods for every API endpoint. Uses httpx internally — the client is an async context manager that manages the HTTP connection pool.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    base_url str

    Base URL of the Orchestration API (e.g. "http://localhost:9100").

    		 required
    token str | None

    Bearer token for authentication (the server's auth_token).

    		 None
    auth_token str | None

    Alias of token, matching the server's argument name.

    		 None
    timeout float

    Default request timeout in seconds.

    		 30.0

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    token and auth_token are both given and differ.

    Use it as an async context manager, or call :meth:aclose when done (the connection pool is opened on first use).

    Example::

    async with OrchestrationClient("http://localhost:9100", token="tok") as c:
    await c.start_process("monitor")
    status = await c.get_process("monitor")
    aclose() async ¶

    Close the HTTP connection pool.

    update_budget(name, **fields) async ¶

    Update budget limits.

    New limits are read at the next budget check (the next tool call, LLM turn or run start); usage counted so far is kept. The response's effective_from says when the change applies and live whether the running process uses it (False when it only applies after a redeploy, e.g. enabled on a process that was built without a budget).

    Example::

    await client.update_budget("monitor", max_cost_per_day=500.0)

    RuntimeTransport¶

    promptise.runtime.distributed.RuntimeTransport ¶

    HTTP management API for an :class:AgentRuntime.

    Exposes REST endpoints for remote process management:

    • GET /health — health check
    • GET /status — full runtime status
    • GET /processes — list all processes
    • GET /processes/{name}/status — single process status
    • POST /processes/{name}/start — start a process
    • POST /processes/{name}/stop — stop a process
    • POST /processes/{name}/restart — restart a process
    • POST /processes/{name}/event — inject a trigger event

    With a coordinator (the node hosting the cluster coordinator):

    • GET /cluster/nodes — the registered nodes and their health
    • POST /cluster/nodes — register (or re-register) a node: {"node_id": ..., "url": ..., "metadata": {...}}; answers 409 with static discovery (the coordinator lists the nodes itself)
    • DELETE /cluster/nodes/{node_id} — unregister a node
    • GET /cluster/status — :meth:RuntimeCoordinator.cluster_status

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    runtime Any

    The :class:AgentRuntime to manage.

    		 required
    host str

    Host to bind to (default 127.0.0.1 — localhost only).

    		 '127.0.0.1'
    port int

    Port to bind to.

    		 9100
    node_id str

    Unique identifier for this node.

    		 'node-1'
    auth_token str | None

    Bearer token required on every endpoint except GET /health: requests must include Authorization: Bearer <token>. Required for a non-loopback host.

    		 None
    allow_unauthenticated bool

    Allow a non-loopback host without auth_token. Only for nodes behind something that authenticates callers itself (an authenticating proxy, a private network you control); anyone who can reach the port can start, stop and drive your agents.

    		 False
    coordinator Any | None

    A :class:RuntimeCoordinator to expose the /cluster routes for (this node hosts the coordinator).

    		 None
    discovery Any | None

    The coordinator's discovery: a :class:RegistryDiscovery (nodes register through POST /cluster/nodes) or a :class:StaticDiscovery.

    		 None
    allowed_node_hosts list[str] | None

    Hosts a registering node's URL may name (*.example.com for subdomains); others get 403. Empty or None: any host.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    auth_token is empty, or host is not a loopback address and there is no auth_token (and allow_unauthenticated is not set).
    node_id property writable ¶

    This node's unique identifier.

    port property ¶

    The port this transport is listening on.

    With port=0 the OS picks a free port; after :meth:start this returns the port actually bound.

    start() async ¶

    Start the HTTP transport server.

    stop() async ¶

    Stop the HTTP transport server.
