    Lifecycle hooks¶

    HookManager¶

    promptise.runtime.hooks.HookManager ¶

    Event-keyed dispatcher for runtime lifecycle hooks.

    Supports per-event registration with optional once semantics, ordered dispatch by priority, per-hook timeouts, exception isolation (one broken hook never blocks the rest), and programmatic deregistration by ID or tag.

    Coroutine safety: all mutation and dispatch are guarded by an asyncio lock. It is safe to register hooks from inside a hook callback. A hook must not await a lifecycle method of the process that dispatched it (stop(), start()): schedule it with asyncio.create_task instead.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    default_timeout float | None

    Seconds a hook may run when it was registered without a timeout (None: no limit, the default for a standalone manager; the manager an :class:AgentProcess creates uses 30 seconds).

    		 None
    clear(event=None) ¶

    Remove all hooks.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    event HookEvent | None

    If provided, clear only this event's hooks; otherwise clear everything.

    		 None
    dispatch(event, *, process_id='', data=None, metadata=None) async ¶

    Fire all hooks registered for event.

    Hooks run in priority order. Exceptions other than :class:HookBlocked are caught, logged, and recorded in the returned :class:DispatchResult — they never propagate to the caller (a fail_closed hook's error also blocks). A hook that exceeds its timeout is cancelled and recorded as an error. HookBlocked short-circuits remaining hooks and returns a blocked result.

    Hooks with once=True are removed from the registry before they run, so each runs at most once, whatever happens.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    event HookEvent

    The event to fire.

    		 required
    process_id str

    Identifier of the dispatching process.

    		 ''
    data dict[str, Any] | None

    Event payload. Hooks get a copy as ctx.data: they may change it in place or assign a new dict to ctx.data (both are honored, and a later hook sees the earlier one's version); what ctx.data holds after the last hook is :attr:DispatchResult.data. For which keys the runtime reads back (e.g. prompt of user_prompt_submit), see :class:HookEvent.

    		 None
    metadata dict[str, Any] | None

    Per-dispatch metadata.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    A DispatchResult
    has_hooks(event) ¶

    Whether any hook is registered for event (cheap; no lock).

    on(event, *, once=False, priority=0, tag=None, timeout=None, fail_closed=False) ¶

    Decorator form of :meth:register.

    Example::

    @hooks.on(HookEvent.USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT)
async def audit(ctx):
    log(ctx.data["prompt"])

@hooks.on(HookEvent.SESSION_START, once=True)
async def greet(ctx):
    print("hello!")
    register(event, callback, *, once=False, priority=0, tag=None, timeout=None, fail_closed=False) ¶

    Register a hook callback for an event.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    event HookEvent | str

    Which :class:HookEvent to subscribe to (or its value, e.g. "session_start").

    		 required
    callback HookCallable

    Async function (or object with an async __call__) taking a single :class:HookContext.

    		 required
    once bool

    If True, the hook auto-deregisters after its first invocation (successful or not). It runs at most once, even when several dispatches of the event overlap.

    		 False
    priority int

    Higher priority hooks run first within an event. Default 0. Use negative priorities to run late.

    		 0
    tag str | None

    Optional string tag for grouped deregistration with :meth:remove_by_tag.

    		 None
    timeout float | None

    Seconds the hook may run (default: the manager's default_timeout). A hook that takes longer is cancelled and recorded as an error.

    		 None
    fail_closed bool

    If True, an error or timeout of this hook blocks the action (for a blockable event) instead of being ignored. Use it for hooks that enforce a policy.

    		 False

    Returns:

    Type Description
    str

    A hook ID suitable for passing to :meth:remove.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TypeError

    callback is not async.
    ValueError

    event is not a :class:HookEvent value, or timeout is not positive.
    registered(event=None) ¶

    Return the hook IDs currently registered.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    event HookEvent | None

    If provided, filter to this event.

    		 None
    remove(hook_id) async ¶

    Deregister a single hook by its ID.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    bool

    True if the hook was found and removed, False otherwise.
    remove_by_tag(tag) async ¶

    Deregister every hook with a matching tag.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    int

    Number of hooks removed.

    HookEvent¶

    promptise.runtime.hooks.HookEvent ¶

    Bases: str, Enum

    Lifecycle events that a :class:HookManager can dispatch.

    There are 13 events. :class:~promptise.runtime.AgentProcess dispatches each of them at the moment described below; ctx.data holds the listed keys (secret values redacted). Events in :data:BLOCKABLE_EVENTS can be refused by raising :class:HookBlocked; for the others a block is logged and ignored. They are deliberately coarse: for per-node / per-tool introspection of a single run, use :mod:promptise.engine.hooks instead.

    HookContext¶

    promptise.runtime.hooks.HookContext dataclass ¶

    Context passed to every hook callback.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    event HookEvent

    The event that is firing.
    process_id str

    Identifier of the :class:AgentProcess dispatching the hook (its name). May be empty for top-level dispatch.
    timestamp datetime

    timezone.utc timestamp of dispatch.
    data dict[str, Any]

    Free-form event payload. Hook implementations may read and (for some events, e.g. USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT) mutate this dict to alter the subsequent runtime behavior; the caller reads it back from :attr:DispatchResult.data.
    metadata dict[str, Any]

    Additional per-dispatch metadata (process_name, process_id), not typically mutated by hooks.
    get(key, default=None) ¶

    Shorthand for self.data.get(key, default).

    set(key, value) ¶

    Shorthand for self.data[key] = value.

    HookBlocked¶

    promptise.runtime.hooks.HookBlocked ¶

    Bases: Exception

    Raised by a hook to block the action that triggered it.

    The dispatcher catches this specifically and returns a blocked=True outcome so callers can abort the in-progress operation (e.g. cancel a tool call, refuse a user prompt). Only the events in :data:BLOCKABLE_EVENTS can be blocked.

    DispatchResult¶

    promptise.runtime.hooks.DispatchResult dataclass ¶

    Outcome of a :meth:HookManager.dispatch call.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    fired int

    Number of hooks that ran.
    blocked bool

    True if any hook raised :class:HookBlocked (or a fail_closed hook failed).
    reason str

    Block reason, if any.
    errors list[tuple[str, Exception]]

    List of (hook_id, exception) tuples for hooks that raised an unexpected exception or timed out. These are logged and swallowed so one broken hook does not take down the runtime.
    data dict[str, Any]

    The event payload after the hooks ran (hooks may mutate it, e.g. rewrite data["prompt"]).

    HookCallable and BLOCKABLE_EVENTS¶

    HookCallable is the type of a hook callback, Callable[[HookContext], Awaitable[None]]. BLOCKABLE_EVENTS is the frozenset of the six HookEvents a hook can refuse: USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT, PERMISSION_REQUEST, SUBAGENT_START, FILE_CHANGED, CONFIG_CHANGE and TASK_CREATED. Both are importable from promptise.runtime. See Runtime Hooks.

    ShellHook¶

    promptise.runtime.shell_hook.ShellHook dataclass ¶

    Runtime hook that shells out to an external command.

    The command receives a JSON event on stdin and may write a JSON response to stdout. Use ShellHook.callback as the callback argument to :meth:HookManager.register.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    command str | list[str]

    The program and its arguments: a list (used as is) or a string (split with :func:shlex.split, so quoting works as in a terminal). With shell=True a string run by /bin/sh -c.
    timeout float

    Max seconds the command may run before being killed. Default 5.0.
    cwd str | None

    Working directory for the subprocess. Default current directory.
    env dict[str, str] | None

    Extra environment variables for the program (added to the minimal environment, see the module docstring). Values may be ${VAR} / ${VAR:-default} references to the host environment, resolved each time the program runs.
    shell bool

    If True, run via the shell instead of an exec. Only for commands written in code: the command string is passed to the shell as is (the payload never is).
    encoding str

    stdin/stdout encoding. Default "utf-8".
    inherit_env bool

    Pass the whole host environment (in 1.4.3 and earlier the default). Off by default so credentials in the environment don't reach hook programs.
    env_passthrough list[str]

    Names of host environment variables to pass through (when set), in addition to :data:SAFE_ENV_VARS.
    max_output_bytes int

    Largest stdout accepted (default 64 KiB); the program is killed and the hook fails beyond it.

    		 
    hook = ShellHook(command="./hooks/audit_prompt.sh")
hooks.register(HookEvent.USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT, hook.callback)

    The script audit_prompt.sh might look like::

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Read JSON from stdin, log the prompt, allow it through.
prompt=$(jq -r .data.prompt)
echo "[$(date)] $prompt" >> /var/log/agent_prompts.log
echo '{}'
    callback(ctx) async ¶

    Async hook callback — pass this to :meth:HookManager.register.

    Serializes the context, runs the command, parses any JSON reply, and applies its directives (mutate ctx.data, raise :class:HookBlocked).

    run(ctx) async ¶

    Execute the underlying command and return the parsed result.

    Public so it can be unit-tested or invoked manually.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TimeoutError

    The program ran longer than timeout.
    RuntimeError

    It exited non-zero.
    ValueError

    Its output was too large or not a JSON object.

    ShellHookResult¶

    promptise.runtime.shell_hook.ShellHookResult dataclass ¶

    Parsed result returned by an external shell hook.

    Dashboard¶

    RuntimeDashboard¶

    promptise.runtime.RuntimeDashboard ¶

    Full-screen tabbed terminal dashboard for the Agent Runtime.

    Follows the same architecture as the MCP server's :class:~promptise.mcp.server._dashboard.Dashboard:

    • 7 tabs -- Overview, Processes, Triggers, Context, Logs, Events, Commands
    • Arrow-key / number-key navigation
    • Live refresh -- ~250ms in a daemon thread
    • Log capture -- Python logger output in Logs tab
    • Command input -- interactive process control

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    state RuntimeDashboardState

    :class:RuntimeDashboardState instance (shared with data collector).

    		 required
    runtime AgentRuntime | None

    Optional :class:AgentRuntime for command execution.

    		 None
    start() ¶

    Start the live dashboard (takes over the terminal).

    Call it from the runtime's event loop (as promptise runtime start --dashboard does): process commands are run on that loop.

    stop() ¶

    Stop the dashboard and restore the terminal.

    RuntimeDashboardState¶

    promptise.runtime.RuntimeDashboardState dataclass ¶

    Thread-safe shared state for the runtime dashboard.

    Mirrors the MCP dashboard's :class:DashboardState pattern but tracks runtime-specific data: processes, triggers, world state, and journal entries.

    record_command(result) ¶

    Record a command executed.

    record_event(event) ¶

    Record a trigger event received.

    record_invocation(log) ¶

    Record a completed agent invocation.

    record_journal(entry) ¶

    Record a journal entry.

    RuntimeDataCollector¶

    promptise.runtime.RuntimeDataCollector ¶

    Collects real-time data from a running AgentRuntime into DashboardState.

    Runs as a background thread, periodically polling the runtime for process status, context state, and trigger info. Trigger events and finished runs arrive through task_created / task_completed hooks it registers on every process (Events and Recent Activity panels, trigger fire counts), and the journal panel is read from each process's journal on the runtime's event loop.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    runtime AgentRuntime

    The runtime to watch.

    		 required
    state RuntimeDashboardState

    The shared dashboard state.

    		 required
    interval float

    Seconds between snapshots.

    		 0.5
    loop AbstractEventLoop | None

    The event loop the runtime runs on (default: the running loop when the collector is created, if any). Without one the journal panel stays empty.

    		 None
    start() ¶

    Start the data collection thread.

    stop() ¶

    Stop collecting and remove the hooks it registered.

    Exceptions¶

    RuntimeBaseError¶

    promptise.runtime.exceptions.RuntimeBaseError ¶

    Bases: RuntimeError

    Base exception for all runtime module errors.

    ProcessStateError¶

    promptise.runtime.exceptions.ProcessStateError ¶

    Bases: RuntimeBaseError

    Raised when a lifecycle state transition is invalid.

    The runtime raises its subclass :class:~promptise.runtime.lifecycle.StateError, which is also a :class:ValueError (what it was in 1.4.3 and earlier), so except ProcessStateError, except StateError and except ValueError all catch an invalid transition.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    process_id

    The process that attempted the transition (None when a :class:~promptise.runtime.lifecycle.StateError was raised without one).
    current_state

    The process's current state.
    attempted_state

    The target state that was rejected.

    ManifestError¶

    promptise.runtime.exceptions.ManifestError ¶

    Bases: RuntimeBaseError

    Raised when .agent manifest loading fails (I/O or parse error).

    ManifestValidationError¶

    promptise.runtime.exceptions.ManifestValidationError ¶

    Bases: ManifestError

    Raised when .agent manifest schema validation fails.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    errors

    Pydantic validation error details (if available).
    file_path

    Path to the manifest file that failed validation.

    ManifestEnvVarError¶

    promptise.runtime.exceptions.ManifestEnvVarError ¶

    Bases: ManifestError, EnvVarNotFoundError

    A ${VAR} in a .agent manifest names an unset environment variable.

    A :class:ManifestError, so the CLI and :meth:AgentRuntime.load_directory report it like any other manifest problem, and an :class:~promptise.exceptions.EnvVarNotFoundError, which is what :func:~promptise.runtime.manifest.load_manifest raised before 1.5.1.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    file_path

    The manifest that references the variable.

    JournalError¶
